title: Evaluate and tune FlashAttention v2/v3 kernels with prefill/decode scheduler
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Background:
We observed variability in token latency and throughput across model families when switching between FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels. Some customer workloads (long-prefill transformer sequences and short decode steps) show regressions in 99th-percentile latency after enabling v3 on H100 for large head_dim models. The runtime's kernel selector currently picks kernels based on hardware and a small heuristic table (seq_len thresholds + head_dim buckets). It does not yet consider the prefill vs decode scheduling differences or mixed-input padding patterns.

Problem statement:
- FlashAttention v3 compiled kernels are faster on many dense workloads but produce worse tail latency in mixed prefill/decode patterns (observed ~12-18% worse p99 for seq_len 2048 prefill + decode batch size 1).
- Some variants crash or produce numerical mismatches with bf16+packed KV cache on H100; rollout to dedicated customers triggered alerts.
- Existing heuristics don't account for: padding ratio, prefix cache reuse, head_dim alignment, and decode latency SLOs.

Goal:
- Identify safe and performant kernel selection rules for v2 and v3 across A100/H100 for our top 10 production models.
- Add scheduler-aware heuristics to prefer kernels that optimize prefill throughput without degrading decode tail latency beyond 5% of current baseline.
- Add CI gating and microbench harnesses to detect regressions automatically.

Proposed approach / work plan:
1) Reproduce: build microbench suite that simulates common prefill+decode patterns (seq_len: 256,512,1024,2048; decode steps: 1..128; batch shapes: 1..32; padding ratios 0%, 25%, 75%). Collect latency/throughput/p99 on A100/H100 with fp16/bf16.
2) Binary diff and numerical checks: run end-to-end inference verification for v2 vs v3 kernels to catch numerical divergence (tolerances: abs<=1e-3 for fp16, compare logits/probs for top-k consistency).
3) Kernel tuning: test head_dim alignments (64/128/192/256) and implement fallback thresholds (e.g., v3 if head_dim % 64==0 and seq_len>=512 and padding_ratio<60%).
4) Scheduler integration: extend kernel-selector to factor in phase (prefill vs decode) and history of prefix reuse; add options to pin decode to lower-latency kernels.
5) Regression protection: add microbench jobs to Perf CI and a canary that runs a subset of top-customer prompts nightly; create alerting if p99 increases >3% vs baseline.
6) Rollout plan: staged rollout -> internal perf-team canary -> small set of Dedicated customers -> region-wide. Provide fallback to previous kernel via config flag.

Acceptance criteria:
- Microbench suite committed and green in CI for both A100 and H100.
- New scheduler can select different kernels for prefill vs decode and has documented heuristics checked into runtime-1.20 branch.
- Benchmarks show no more than 5% regression in p99 for top-10 models; median latency and tokens/sec improve or are neutral.
- Nightly canary job with alerting is configured and linked to runbook.
- Two code reviews: runtime change and perf harness.

Notes on risk and trade-offs:
- Aggressive selection of v3 yields best median throughput but may harm decode tail latency. We need to prioritize decode p99 for low-latency chat use-cases.
- Numerical divergence risk: v3 uses different accumulation/tiling; keep numerical checks and a safety toggle to force v2 for sensitive customers.
- Complexity: increasing heuristic dimensions makes maintenance harder; we'll add telemetry to measure selection frequency and a dashboard to adjust thresholds.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Microbench suite integrated into Perf CI and green on A100 and H100.
2) Kernel-selector updated to use scheduling-aware heuristics (prefill vs decode).
3) p99 regressions <=5% for top-10 models vs baseline.
4) Canary + alerting in place, runbook documented.
5) Runtime flag to force fallback to v2 and documentation for ops.
